title: Efficient Deep Ensemble Inference via Query Difficulty-dependent Task Scheduling
motivation: Deep ensemble inference causes high deadline miss rates (45% during traffic bursts) in latency-sensitive tasks, with existing approaches ignoring deadline constraints
problem_framing: Scheduling problem: dynamically assign subsets of base models to queries based on predicted difficulty and queuing status to maximize accuracy under deadline constraints
key_insight: 78.3% of samples can be correctly predicted by any single base model; only <11% require all models, indicating massive redundancy exploitable via difficulty-dependent scheduling
method_signature: Discrepancy score predicts query difficulty; dynamic programming scheduler assigns model subsets based on accuracy reward maximization
evaluation_criteria: Deadline miss rate and accuracy under deadline constraints on text matching, vehicle counting, and image retrieval tasks
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Static selection results in bad trade-offs (huge accuracy loss OR high miss rate); DES/Gating fail to capture deep model preferences due to high variance and ignore queuing status
evidence_for_taste: 78.3% samples predicted correctly by any model
deadline miss rate reaches 45% during traffic burst
gating network outputs similar weights for all samples
existing approaches select models regardless of queue status
preferences of deep models are complicated and hard to capture
thinking_moves: 从实际系统瓶颈(deadline miss)反推问题定义
引入discrepancy score替代ensemble agreement解决heterogeneous模型问题
将调度问题分解为local subproblems并用DP求解
通过竞争比分析证明算法最优性下界
对Gating失败原因做ablation式分析(偏好空间高方差)
